description.narrative: “Implementation of e-Procurement and e-Procurement Capacity Building” The Government of Tajikistan (GoT) has been continuously reforming and modernizing the public procurement. The initial reform work started in 1995. Since then the public procurement system has considerably evolved and today the government is moving ahead with decentralization by capacity building and modernizing through e-procurement. The GoT has established the Agency on State Procurement of Goodscomma Works and Services (ASP) as an Independent Public Procurement Regulatory Body. The introduction of e-Procurement will help to ensure transparency & efficiency of public procurement procedures. Recently the GOT has adopted an e-Procurement Program for 2013 - 2015. The GoT made a first step towards e-Procurement implementation in Tajikistan by using its own internal resources (allocated US$ 60comma000). The GoT designed web portal where procurement-related information such as the Public Procurement Lawcomma procurement noticescomma and contract award data is disclosed. The ASP leads the e-Procurement agenda and continues to learn from other countries about the opportunities and challenges of e-Procurement implementation. In this directioncomma the ASP has introduced e-quotation module to pilot e-GP that started functioning since March 2013. This shows commitment from the GoT to achieve modern procurement system including e-GP. The World Bank provides systematic support to the GoT through different activities. The Country Procurement Status Review (CPSR) jointly conducted with the ADB was completed recently to carry out a broad assessment of Tajikistan’s public procurement system. Based on the reviewcomma the Bank made recommendations to the GoT to strengthen the public procurement system performance.
